newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.60/2.55 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.53/2.48 percent but one-year was unchanged from Monday's yield of 2.18/2.13 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.00/98.05 against Monday's close of S$99.28/99.33, September 2001 at S$97.93/97.98 versus S$99.30/99.35 and June 2003 at S$96.90/96.95 from S$98.82/98.87.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Monday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
